chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi Khalid al-Ash'ari, who said:

One of our companions wrote to Abū Ja'far al-Thānī عليه السلام through me, asking him about a man who committed fornication with a woman and she became pregnant. Then he married her after the pregnancy, and she gave birth to a child, and the child resembled him more than anyone in Allah's creation.
So he عليه السلام wrote in his own handwriting and with his seal: “The child is of fornication and does not inherit.”

key_terms.الْوَلَدُ لِغَيَّةٍ: the child is legally classified as born of fornication
key_terms.بَعْدَ الْحَمْلِ: after the pregnancy had already occurred
key_terms.بِخَطِّهِ وَخَاتَمِهِ: in the Imam’s own handwriting and bearing his seal

ai.seo_question: Does a child conceived through zina inherit if the parents marry afterward?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a child conceived through zina before the man later married the woman. Imam Abū Ja'far al-Thānī عليه السلام states that such a child is deemed a child of fornication and does not inherit, even if the child strongly resembles the man.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5681 - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Abi Khalid Al-Ash'ari, who said:

One of our companions wrote to Abu Ja'far Al-Thani (as) through me, asking Imam (as) about a man who committed adultery with a woman, and she became pregnant. Later, he married her after the pregnancy, and she gave birth to a child who resembled him more than anyone else in creation.

Imam (as) wrote back in his own handwriting and with his seal:
"The child is the result of fornication and does not inherit."
